en: The Ritual for Paying Homage to the Lotus Sūtra:

With single-minded devotion, prostrate to the eternally abiding Triple Gem throughout the ten directions and the entire Dharma-realm. Rising from the prostration, kneel with palms joined, burn incense, and perform mental visualization. Then, with palms joined, chant:
"May these clouds of incense and flowers pervade the worlds of the ten directions, making offerings to all Buddhas and the wondrous Dharma."
The Lotus Sūtra.
The assembly of Bodhisattvas and Śrāvakas,
receiving it as a Buddha-work, rose from their prostrations and exclaimed:

I prostrate to the Buddhas of the ten directions, who have perfected the Supreme Vehicle and opened the two gates of the original and the manifested; through Dharma and parables they discourse upon the true mystery,
universally enabling all those of provisional and limited capacities to realize the Bodhi of the Buddha.
I now vow to take refuge; may I transcend the ocean of birth and death.
Having offered praise, I shall now express my sincere intentions as I wish.
Although this is called the "Ritual Classic," one ought nevertheless to pay homage to the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas,
so that the meaning of the Three Jewels may be fulfilled.
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to our original teacher, Śākyamuni Buddha.
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to the past Buddha Prabhūtaratna.
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to the emanations of Śākyamuni Buddha throughout the ten directions.
With single-minded devotion, I prostrate to all Buddhas throughout the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra* and in the ten directions and three periods of time;
with single-minded devotion, I prostrate to the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra*.
For each character of the Dharma-treasure of the wondrous syllables below, chant once and prostrate once.
With single-minded devotion, pay homage to all Bodhisattvas, Śrāvakas, Pratyekabuddhas,
and noble Sangha of those who have attained the Way throughout the ten directions and the three periods of time, as contained within the entire *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra*.

With single-minded devotion, prostrate to Samantabhadra Bodhisattva Mahāsattva. Having prostrated, kneel with the right knee on the ground and perform the visualization according to the standard ritual.
With a sincere heart, repent:
I, [Name], together with all sentient beings, from time immemorial...
Having lost the true mind, they wander through the cycle of birth and death;
their karmic obstacles of the six sense organs are immeasurable and boundless,
and thus they lack the means to open their understanding of the Perfect and Wondrous Buddha Vehicle.
May all my aspirations be fulfilled; I now pay homage to the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra*.
By this root of goodness, I confess and reveal all dark and evil deeds committed through the three karmas of body, speech, and mind in the past, present, and future.
Boundless grave offenses shall all be extinguished;
body and mind will become pure, and afflictions and hindrances will be eliminated;
adorned with merit and wisdom, the causes for purification will increase.
May the practices and vows of myself and others be swiftly and perfectly fulfilled.
May all Tathāgatas remain forever preaching the Dharma.
Regarding all such merits, may I give rise to a mind of sympathetic joy.
Dedicating this toward Bodhi, one realizes the fruit of eternal bliss;
on the day of death, right mindfulness manifests before them,
and they personally behold Amitābha and the assembly of holy beings.
In a single instant, one is born within a lotus flower.
Having performed repentance and made vows, universally wishing that all sentient beings may together attain the Buddha-way,
one takes refuge and pays homage to the Triple Gem.

Homage to the Buddha. Homage to the Dharma. Homage to the Saṃgha. Homage to Śākyamuni Buddha. Homage to the Lotus Sūtra of the Wondrous Dharma. Homage to Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva. Homage to Samantabhadra Bodhisattva. Having completed the circumambulation, perform the threefold refuge according to the usual ritual procedures for the Lotus Sūtra.
